concept.name: Volume divergence
concept.definition: A discrepancy in which price registers a new extreme while volume fails to confirm it — for example a higher high made on noticeably lower volume than the prior high — read in Wyckoff and volume-spread practice as diminishing effort behind the trend. It is a warning heuristic, not a stand-alone timing signal.
concept.intuition: If each new push in the trend direction attracts fewer participants, the move may be running out of fuel even while price still advances.
concept.mechanics: Volume on successive price extremes in the same direction is compared, or volume on rallies versus reactions across a range; a declining volume trend against advancing price constitutes the divergence and prompts closer scrutiny of subsequent price behavior.
concept.failure_modes: Trends — especially grinding, low-volatility advances — can persist for long stretches on declining volume, so acting on divergence alone is a classic way to fade strong trends prematurely.
concept.misconceptions: Volume divergence is not a reversal trigger; practitioners treat it as context that must be confirmed by price behavior such as failure to make further progress or absorption at the extreme.
concept.example: A future makes three successive swing highs at 4,510, 4,522 and 4,530 while swing volume falls from 1.2M to 0.9M to 0.6M contracts — a bearish volume divergence flagged for monitoring, not an automatic short.
